q: 那是李老师___自行车，不是我的。
zh: 那是李老师的自行车，不是我的。
py: nà shì lǐ lǎo shī de zì xíng chē bú shì wǒ de
en: That is Teacher Li's bike, not mine.
why: A named owner before an ordinary thing needs 的: 李老师的自行车. Leaving it out gives no normal phrase, and 得 is a different de that follows verbs.

q: 你看见小王___书包了吗？
zh: 你看见小王的书包了吗？
py: nǐ kàn jiàn xiǎo wáng de shū bāo le ma
en: Have you seen Xiao Wang's school bag?
why: Owner + 的 + thing: 小王的书包. Without 的 the owner and the bag do not link, and 地 only attaches to adverbs before a verb.

q: 请告诉我你___地址和电话号码。
zh: 请告诉我你的地址和电话号码。
py: qǐng gào su wǒ nǐ de dì zhǐ hé diàn huà hào mǎ
en: Please tell me your address and phone number.
why: A pronoun before an ordinary thing such as an address takes 的: 你的地址. 们 would make 'you (plural)', which is not the meaning here.

q: 邻居___狗每天早上都在门口叫。
zh: 邻居的狗每天早上都在门口叫。
py: lín ju de gǒu měi tiān zǎo shàng dōu zài mén kǒu jiào
en: The neighbour's dog barks at the door every morning.
why: Noun owner + 的 + thing: 邻居的狗. A neighbour is not kin or a group you belong to, so 的 cannot be dropped.

q: 出租车司机___名字我没记住。
zh: 出租车司机的名字我没记住。
py: chū zū chē sī jī de míng zi wǒ méi jì zhù
en: I did not remember the taxi driver's name.
why: Owner first, then 的, then the thing owned: 司机的名字. 地 marks an adverb and does not link an owner to a noun.

q: 老板___办公室在三楼，他今天出差了，你下午再来吧。
zh: 老板的办公室在三楼，他今天出差了，你下午再来吧。
py: lǎo bǎn de bàn gōng shì zài sān lóu tā jīn tiān chū chāi le nǐ xià wǔ zài lái ba
en: The boss's office is on the third floor, but he is away on business today, so come back this afternoon.
why: Owner + 的 + place: 老板的办公室. 得 follows verbs and 地 goes before verbs, so neither can link a person to a noun.

q: 我___学校有两个图书馆。
zh: 我们学校有两个图书馆。
py: wǒ men xué xiào yǒu liǎng gè tú shū guǎn
en: Our school has two libraries.
why: For a school you belong to, say 我们学校: plural pronoun, no 的. 个 is a measure word and 了 marks a change; neither can follow 我 here.

q: 我___公司有五百个人。
zh: 我们公司有五百个人。
py: wǒ men gōng sī yǒu wǔ bǎi gè rén
en: Our company has five hundred people.
why: A company you belong to is 我们公司, plural pronoun and no 的. 个 is a measure word and 了 marks a change; neither can follow 我 here.

q: 这是我妈妈___朋友。
zh: 这是我妈妈的朋友。
py: zhè shì wǒ mā ma de péng you
en: This is a friend of my mother's.
why: In a chain only the last link keeps 的: 我妈妈的朋友. Without 的 the chain is incomplete, and 们 would make the mother plural.

q: 我哥哥___车是新的。
zh: 我哥哥的车是新的。
py: wǒ gē ge de chē shì xīn de
en: My older brother's car is new.
why: The pronoun drops 的 before 哥哥, but the last link before 车 keeps it: 我哥哥的车. Dropping it would glue 哥哥 and 车 together wrongly.

q: 我姐姐___男朋友在银行工作。
zh: 我姐姐的男朋友在银行工作。
py: wǒ jiě jie de nán péng you zài yín háng gōng zuò
en: My older sister's boyfriend works at a bank.
why: Pronoun + kin has no 的, but kin + the person described needs it: 我姐姐的男朋友. 们 is not needed because there is one sister.

q: 我奶奶___邻居昨天送来了一篮子苹果，我们全家都很感谢她。
zh: 我奶奶的邻居昨天送来了一篮子苹果，我们全家都很感谢她。
py: wǒ nǎi nai de lín ju zuó tiān sòng lái le yī lán zi píng guǒ wǒ men quán jiā dōu hěn gǎn xiè tā
en: My grandmother's neighbour brought a basket of apples yesterday, and our whole family is grateful to her.
why: Chain of owners: 我 + 奶奶 drops 的, but 奶奶 + 邻居 keeps it: 我奶奶的邻居. The last link before the noun always carries 的.

q: 她是一个很好___老师。
zh: 她是一个很好的老师。
py: tā shì yí gè hěn hǎo de lǎo shī
en: She is a very good teacher.
why: Once 很 stands before the adjective it is a phrase, and a phrase needs 的 before the noun: 很好的老师. Bare 好老师 would not take 很.

q: 这是我们这儿最大___超市。
zh: 这是我们这儿最大的超市。
py: zhè shì wǒ men zhè r zuì dà de chāo shì
en: This is the biggest supermarket here.
why: 最 + adjective is a phrase, so 的 is required: 最大的超市. Without it the degree word has nothing linking it to 超市.

q: 我想找一个很安静___地方看书。
zh: 我想找一个很安静的地方看书。
py: wǒ xiǎng zhǎo yí gè hěn ān jìng de dì fang kàn shū
en: I want to find a very quiet place to read.
why: 很安静 is a degree word + two-syllable adjective, so 的 links it to 地方. 地 attaches to adverbs before verbs, not to nouns.

q: 这是这条街上最贵___饭店。
zh: 这是这条街上最贵的饭店。
py: zhè shì zhè tiáo jiē shàng zuì guì de fàn diàn
en: This is the most expensive restaurant on this street.
why: 最贵 describes the noun, so 的 must close it: 最贵的饭店. 得 follows verbs and cannot join an adjective to a noun.

q: 妈妈买了一张非常漂亮___桌布。
zh: 妈妈买了一张非常漂亮的桌布。
py: mā ma mǎi le yī zhāng fēi cháng piào liang de zhuō bù
en: Mum bought a very pretty tablecloth.
why: 非常漂亮 is a degree word plus a two-syllable adjective, so 的 is required before 桌布. 地 would turn it into an adverb.

q: 我们住在一个干净又安静___小区。
zh: 我们住在一个干净又安静的小区。
py: wǒ men zhù zài yí gè gān jìng yòu ān jìng de xiǎo qū
en: We live in a clean and quiet neighbourhood.
why: A list of adjectives joined by 又 is a phrase and needs 的 before the noun: 干净又安静的小区. Bare adjectives joined by 又 cannot attach directly.

q: 爸爸给我们做了很辣___菜，我吃不了。
zh: 爸爸给我们做了很辣的菜，我吃不了。
py: bà ba gěi wǒ men zuò le hěn là de cài wǒ chī bù liǎo
en: Dad made a very spicy dish for us and I cannot eat it.
why: 很辣 is degree word + adjective, so 的 links it to 菜. 得 would follow the verb 做, not precede the noun.

q: 这是一条人很多、车也很多___马路，过马路的时候一定要小心。
zh: 这是一条人很多、车也很多的马路，过马路的时候一定要小心。
py: zhè shì yī tiáo rén hěn duō chē yě hěn duō de mǎ lù guò mǎ lù de shí hou yí dìng yào xiǎo xīn
en: This is a road with lots of people and lots of cars, so be careful when you cross.
why: A whole description (人很多、车也很多) before a noun must end in 的: ...的马路. Without it the clause does not attach to 马路.

q: 他是一个热情又有耐心___邻居，经常帮奶奶拿东西。
zh: 他是一个热情又有耐心的邻居，经常帮奶奶拿东西。
py: tā shì yí gè rè qíng yòu yǒu nài xīn de lín ju jīng cháng bāng nǎi nai ná dōng xi
en: He is a warm and patient neighbour who often carries things for Grandma.
why: A pair of descriptions joined by 又 forms a phrase, so 的 comes before 邻居. 地 only goes before verbs.

q: 妈妈做___菜最好吃。
zh: 妈妈做的菜最好吃。
py: mā ma zuò de cài zuì hǎo chī
en: The food Mum cooks tastes the best.
why: A verb phrase before a noun must end in 的: 妈妈做的菜. Putting 了 there would not link 做 to 菜.

q: 我昨天买___书很贵。
zh: 我昨天买的书很贵。
py: wǒ zuó tiān mǎi de shū hěn guì
en: The book I bought yesterday was expensive.
why: Clause + 的 + noun: 我昨天买的书. Without 的 the clause is not turned into a description of 书, and 过 means 'ever bought'.

q: 喜欢喝茶___人很多。
zh: 喜欢喝茶的人很多。
py: xǐ huan hē chá de rén hěn duō
en: Many people like drinking tea.
why: The verb phrase 喜欢喝茶 describes 人, so it ends in 的. 了 or 地 would not join it to the noun.

q: 我们吃饭___地方在学校旁边。
zh: 我们吃饭的地方在学校旁边。
py: wǒ men chī fàn de dì fang zài xué xiào páng biān
en: The place where we eat is next to the school.
why: Clause + 的 + 地方 gives 'the place where...': 我们吃饭的地方. There is no word for 'where' in this pattern.

q: 这是我奶奶小时候住___房子。
zh: 这是我奶奶小时候住的房子。
py: zhè shì wǒ nǎi nai xiǎo shí hou zhù de fáng zi
en: This is the house my grandmother lived in as a child.
why: A clause describing 房子 must end in 的: 小时候住的房子. 住过房子 would stop at 'lived in a house' and leave 这是 without a noun phrase.

q: 我想找一个能一起练习口语___同学。
zh: 我想找一个能一起练习口语的同学。
py: wǒ xiǎng zhǎo yí gè néng yì qǐ liàn xí kǒu yǔ de tóng xué
en: I want to find a classmate I can practise speaking with.
why: The clause 能一起练习口语 describes 同学 and ends in 的. 得 is the complement marker that follows verbs and cannot do this.

q: 坐在沙发上看电视___那个人是我爸爸。
zh: 坐在沙发上看电视的那个人是我爸爸。
py: zuò zài shā fā shàng kàn diàn shì de nà ge rén shì wǒ bà ba
en: The person sitting on the sofa watching TV is my dad.
why: The whole clause goes before 那个人 and ends in 的. 着 or 了 would leave a bare verb phrase with no link to 人.

q: 从地铁站到我家___路不太远。
zh: 从地铁站到我家的路不太远。
py: cóng dì tiě zhàn dào wǒ jiā de lù bù tài yuǎn
en: The way from the metro station to my home is not very far.
why: A phrase before a noun takes 的: 从地铁站到我家的路. 地 is for adverbs, and 了 marks an event, not a description.

q: 去图书馆___公共汽车在哪儿坐？
zh: 去图书馆的公共汽车在哪儿坐？
py: qù tú shū guǎn de gōng gòng qì chē zài nǎ r zuò
en: Where do I catch the bus that goes to the library?
why: 去图书馆 describes the bus, so it ends in 的: 去图书馆的公共汽车. Without 的 it would read as a separate action.

q: 我昨天在商店门口遇到___人是你哥哥以前的同学。
zh: 我昨天在商店门口遇到的人是你哥哥以前的同学。
py: wǒ zuó tiān zài shāng diàn mén kǒu yù dào de rén shì nǐ gē ge yǐ qián de tóng xué
en: The person I met at the shop door yesterday was your brother's former classmate.
why: The clause 我昨天在商店门口遇到 ends in 的 and sits before 人. 了 or 过 would leave the clause unlinked to 人.

q: 我们刚搬进去___那套房子离地铁站只有五分钟。
zh: 我们刚搬进去的那套房子离地铁站只有五分钟。
py: wǒ men gāng bān jìn qù de nà tào fáng zi lí dì tiě zhàn zhǐ yǒu wǔ fēn zhōng
en: The flat we just moved into is only five minutes from the metro station.
why: 搬进去的 describes 那套房子: clause + 的 + noun. 地 goes before verbs, and 了 would leave 搬进去 as a separate verb.

q: 这本书是我___，那本是他的。
zh: 这本书是我的，那本是他的。
py: zhè běn shū shì wǒ de nà běn shì tā de
en: This book is mine; that one is his.
why: With the noun understood, 的 stands in for it: 我的 means 'mine'. 这本书是我 would say 'this book is me'.

q: 这件衣服太小了，我要大___。
zh: 这件衣服太小了，我要大的。
py: zhè jiàn yī fu tài xiǎo le wǒ yào dà de
en: This piece of clothing is too small; I want the bigger one.
why: 大的 means 'the big one'; 的 stands for the missing noun. An English-style 'one' is not added, and bare 大 cannot be an object.

q: 冰箱里有吃___吗？
zh: 冰箱里有吃的吗？
py: bīng xiāng lǐ yǒu chī de ma
en: Is there anything to eat in the fridge?
why: Verb + 的 turns the verb into a thing: 吃的 is 'something to eat'. 地 and 得 do not make nouns.

q: 这个杯子是谁___？
zh: 这个杯子是谁的？
py: zhè ge bēi zi shì shéi de
en: Whose cup is this?
why: 'Whose' is 谁的, and 的 keeps the meaning of an owner. 谁 alone would ask 'who is this cup', and 们 does not fit a singular question.

q: 这不是我昨天买___，是姐姐买的。
zh: 这不是我昨天买的，是姐姐买的。
py: zhè bú shì wǒ zuó tiān mǎi de shì jiě jie mǎi de
en: This is not the one I bought yesterday; my sister bought it.
why: 我昨天买的 means 'the one I bought yesterday', with the noun dropped but 的 kept. 买了 would end the clause without a noun to point to.

q: 外面很冷，你带点穿___吧。
zh: 外面很冷，你带点穿的吧。
py: wài miàn hěn lěng nǐ dài diǎn chuān de ba
en: It's cold outside, so bring something to wear.
why: Verb + 的 means 'something to wear': 穿的. 着 or 了 would leave 穿 as a bare verb with nothing for 带点 to carry.

q: 我的手机没电了，可以用你___吗？
zh: 我的手机没电了，可以用你的吗？
py: wǒ de shǒu jī méi diàn le kě yǐ yòng nǐ de ma
en: My phone is out of power; may I use yours?
why: Owner + 的 means 'yours': 你的. 用你 would mean 'use you', so the possessive 的 must stay when the noun is dropped.

q: 沙发上的书，红皮的是我的，蓝皮___是姐姐的。
zh: 沙发上的书，红皮的是我的，蓝皮的是姐姐的。
py: shā fā shàng de shū hóng pí de shì wǒ de lán pí de shì jiě jie de
en: Of the books on the sofa, the red-covered one is mine and the blue-covered one is my sister's.
why: The pattern 红皮的 / 蓝皮的 uses 的 for the dropped noun, and the second half must match it. 蓝皮 alone cannot be a subject meaning 'the blue one'.

q: 我们家的两辆车，白色那辆是爸爸___，黑色的是妈妈的。
zh: 我们家的两辆车，白色那辆是爸爸的，黑色的是妈妈的。
py: wǒ men jiā de liǎng liàng chē bái sè nà liàng shì bà ba de hēi sè de shì mā ma de
en: Of our family's two cars, the white one is Dad's and the black one is Mum's.
why: With the noun 车 understood, 爸爸的 means 'Dad's'. 爸爸 alone would say 'the white one is Dad', which is the wrong meaning.

q: 我昨天买的___书在桌子上。
zh: 我昨天买的那本书在桌子上。
py: wǒ zuó tiān mǎi de nà běn shū zài zhuō zi shàng
en: That book I bought yesterday is on the table.
why: A clause + 那 + measure word + noun is the normal order, and the measure for a single 书 is 本. 那些 is plural, and 那本的 wrongly adds 的 after the measure word.

q: 我有___会说中文的同事。
zh: 我有一个会说中文的同事。
py: wǒ yǒu yí gè huì shuō zhōng wén de tóng shì
en: I have a colleague who can speak Chinese.
why: A new item is introduced with 一个 before the clause: 一个会说中文的同事. 哪个 is a question word and 几个的 puts 的 after a measure word.

q: 我的___孩子都在北京工作，只有小女儿在家。
zh: 我的两个孩子都在北京工作，只有小女儿在家。
py: wǒ de liǎng gè hái zi dōu zài běi jīng gōng zuò zhǐ yǒu xiǎo nǚ ér zài jiā
en: My two children both work in Beijing; only the youngest daughter is at home.
why: Owner first, then number + measure + noun: 我的两个孩子. 的 never follows a measure word, and a bare 两 needs a measure word.

q: 我买了三本___书。
zh: 我买了三本书。
py: wǒ mǎi le sān běn shū
en: I bought three books.
why: A number + measure word attaches straight to the noun: 三本书. 的 after the measure word is never used, and 个 after 本 would double the measure word.

q: 这个___人我不认识。
zh: 这个人我不认识。
py: zhè ge rén wǒ bù rèn shi
en: I do not know this person.
why: 这个 already points straight at the noun, so nothing goes between 个 and 人. 这个的人 is a classic learner error.

q: 我家有两只___猫，一只白的，一只黑的。
zh: 我家有两只猫，一只白的，一只黑的。
py: wǒ jiā yǒu liǎng zhǐ māo yī zhī bái de yī zhī hēi de
en: We have two cats at home, a white one and a black one.
why: Number + measure + noun takes no 的: 两只猫. 们 does not combine with a number, and 的 after 只 is wrong.

q: 请给我一杯___水。
zh: 请给我一杯水。
py: qǐng gěi wǒ yī bēi shuǐ
en: Please give me a glass of water.
why: 一杯水 is number + measure + noun with no 的 in between. 一杯的水 would mean something different and unnatural here.

q: 我有一些___问题想问老师。
zh: 我有一些问题想问老师。
py: wǒ yǒu yī xiē wèn tí xiǎng wèn lǎo shī
en: I have some questions I want to ask the teacher.
why: 一些 works like a measure word and attaches directly to the noun: 一些问题. 一些的问题 is not used.

q: 那张___桌子是爸爸买的。
zh: 那张桌子是爸爸买的。
py: nà zhāng zhuō zi shì bà ba mǎi de
en: That table was bought by Dad.
why: 那 + measure word + noun takes no 的: 那张桌子. Putting 的 after 张 is the typical error.

q: 你想去哪家___饭店吃饭？
zh: 你想去哪家饭店吃饭？
py: nǐ xiǎng qù nǎ jiā fàn diàn chī fàn
en: Which restaurant do you want to eat at?
why: 哪 + measure word attaches straight to the noun: 哪家饭店. 的 never follows 家 here.

q: 我们家有三个___房间，一个是我的。
zh: 我们家有三个房间，一个是我的。
py: wǒ men jiā yǒu sān gè fáng jiān yí gè shì wǒ de
en: Our home has three rooms, one of which is mine.
why: 三个房间 is number + measure + noun with no 的. The later 我的 is a separate use of 的 for a dropped noun.

q: 路口那座___大楼是新建的医院，听说下个月开门。
zh: 路口那座大楼是新建的医院，听说下个月开门。
py: lù kǒu nà zuò dà lóu shì xīn jiàn de yī yuàn tīng shuō xià gè yuè kāi mén
en: The big building at the junction is the newly built hospital, and I hear it opens next month.
why: 那座大楼 attaches 那 + measure to the noun with no 的. A second measure word such as 个 cannot be stacked after 座.

q: 这几天我看了好几部___电影，都不错。
zh: 这几天我看了好几部电影，都不错。
py: zhè jǐ tiān wǒ kàn le hǎo jǐ bù diàn yǐng dōu bù cuò
en: These last few days I watched quite a few films, and all were good.
why: 好几部电影 is a number phrase + measure + noun and takes no 的. 好几部的电影 is a wrong addition after the measure word.

q: 我买了几件___衣服，打算过年的时候送给爸爸妈妈。
zh: 我买了几件衣服，打算过年的时候送给爸爸妈妈。
py: wǒ mǎi le jǐ jiàn yī fu dǎ suàn guò nián de shí hou sòng gěi bà ba mā ma
en: I bought a few pieces of clothing to give to my parents at New Year.
why: 几件衣服: 几 + measure + noun with no 的. A 的 after 件 would not be said by native speakers.

zh: 那是李老师的自行车。
py: nà shì lǐ lǎo shī de zì xíng chē
en: That is Teacher Li's bike.
why: Owner + 的 + thing: 李老师的自行车. The owner cannot follow the bike, as the English 'of' order would suggest.

zh: 我妈妈的朋友是医生。
py: wǒ mā ma de péng you shì yī shēng
en: My mother's friend is a doctor.
why: Pronoun + kin has no 的, and only the last link keeps it: 我妈妈的朋友. 我的 would be redundant in a chain like this.

zh: 她是一个很好的老师。
py: tā shì yí gè hěn hǎo de lǎo shī
en: She is a very good teacher.
why: 很好 is a phrase, so it must be followed by 的 before 老师. 一个 usually comes first, though spoken Chinese also allows 很好的一个老师.

zh: 我昨天买的书很贵。
py: wǒ zuó tiān mǎi de shū hěn guì
en: The book I bought yesterday was expensive.
why: The whole clause 我昨天买 comes before 书 and ends in 的. It cannot follow 书, as English 'that I bought' would.

zh: 妈妈做的菜最好吃。
py: mā ma zuò de cài zuì hǎo chī
en: The food Mum makes is the most delicious.
why: 妈妈做 + 的 + 菜 builds 'the food Mum makes'. 最好吃 is the predicate for the whole phrase and cannot stand before 菜.

zh: 我们吃饭的地方在学校旁边。
py: wǒ men chī fàn de dì fang zài xué xiào páng biān
en: The place where we eat is next to the school.
why: Clause + 的 + place noun: 我们吃饭的地方. There is no 'where' word, and the clause cannot come after 地方.

zh: 去火车站的公共汽车在那边坐。
py: qù huǒ chē zhàn de gōng gòng qì chē zài nà biān zuò
en: You catch the bus to the train station over there.
why: 去火车站 + 的 describes the bus and must precede it. 在那边 stays before the verb 坐; the whole bus phrase may also come last: 在那边坐去火车站的公共汽车.

zh: 我的两个朋友都在上海工作。
py: wǒ de liǎng gè péng you dōu zài shàng hǎi gōng zuò
en: Two of my friends both work in Shanghai.
why: Owner + 的 first, then number + measure + noun: 我的两个朋友. 两个我的朋友 reverses the order and is wrong.

zh: 我昨天买的那本书在桌子上。
py: wǒ zuó tiān mǎi de nà běn shū zài zhuō zi shàng
en: That book I bought yesterday is on the table.
why: The clause goes before 那本 and 书, so the normal order is 我昨天买的那本书. 那本我昨天买的书 is also possible but less common.

zh: 我昨天看了一部很有意思的电影。
py: wǒ zuó tiān kàn le yī bù hěn yǒu yì si de diàn yǐng
en: I watched a very interesting film yesterday.
why: A new item takes 一部 first, then the description + 的 before 电影. A spoken variant puts 一部 after 的, but 的 never follows the measure word.

zh: 姐姐买了几件衣服。
py: jiě jie mǎi le jǐ jiàn yī fu
en: My sister bought a few pieces of clothing.
why: 几件 attaches straight to 衣服. A learner may feel a link is missing, but 的 is never added after a measure word.

zh: 这把钥匙是我的，那把是哥哥的。
py: zhè bǎ yào shi shì wǒ de nà bǎ shì gē ge de
en: This key is mine, and that one is my brother's.
why: 我的 and 哥哥的 keep 的 because the noun 钥匙 has been dropped. Without 的 the sentence would say 'this key is me'.

zh: 冰箱里有吃的也有喝的。
py: bīng xiāng lǐ yǒu chī de yě yǒu hē de
en: There is something to eat and something to drink in the fridge.
why: 吃的 and 喝的 are verb + 的 nominals meaning 'things to eat / drink'. The two halves can swap places with the same meaning.

zh: 这是这条街上最贵的饭店。
py: zhè shì zhè tiáo jiē shàng zuì guì de fàn diàn
en: This is the most expensive restaurant on this street.
why: 最 + adjective needs 的 before the noun: 最贵的饭店. The degree word stays directly before the adjective, never after it.

zh: 我哥哥的朋友住在我们学校旁边。
py: wǒ gē ge de péng you zhù zài wǒ men xué xiào páng biān
en: My older brother's friend lives next to our school.
why: Two kin or group links: 我哥哥 and 我们学校 drop 的, but 哥哥 + 朋友 needs it. The noun 学校 gets no 的 after 我们.

src_py: mā ma zuò cài cài hěn hǎo chī
task: Join into one sentence: "The food Mum cooks is delicious."
zh: 妈妈做的菜很好吃。
py: mā ma zuò de cài hěn hǎo chī
en: The food Mum cooks is delicious.
why: The verb phrase 妈妈做 moves in front of 菜 and ends in 的, so the second clause no longer repeats the noun.

zh: 这是我的。
py: zhè shì wǒ de
en: This is mine.
why: Possessive + 的 can stand alone for the noun. 我 without 的 would not mean 'mine'.

src_py: wǒ xiǎng yào hóng sè de yī fu
task: Drop the noun: "I want the red one."
zh: 我想要红色的。
py: wǒ xiǎng yào hóng sè de
en: I want the red one.
why: With the noun 衣服 understood, 红色的 means 'the red one'. 的 stays; no word for 'one' is added.

src_py: tā shì gè hǎo lǎo shī
task: Make it "a very good teacher" with 很.
zh: 她是个很好的老师。
py: tā shì gè hěn hǎo de lǎo shī
en: She is a very good teacher.
why: Once 很 stands before the adjective, 的 is needed before 老师. 很好老师 is the classic learner error.

src_py: zhè shì jiě jie de shǒu jī
task: Turn it into a question: "Whose phone is this?"
zh: 这是谁的手机？
py: zhè shì shéi de shǒu jī
en: Whose phone is this?
why: 谁 takes the place of 姐姐 and keeps the 的: 这是谁的手机. With the noun first, 这手机是谁的 also works.

src: 我的朋友的姐姐在医院工作。
src_py: wǒ de péng you de jiě jie zài yī yuàn gōng zuò
task: Keep only one 的: "My friend's older sister works at a hospital."
zh: 我朋友的姐姐在医院工作。
py: wǒ péng you de jiě jie zài yī yuàn gōng zuò
en: My friend's older sister works at a hospital.
why: In a chain of owners the 的 after the pronoun is dropped and only the last link keeps it: 我朋友的姐姐.

src: 我姐姐昨天做了一个蛋糕，蛋糕很好吃。
src_py: wǒ jiě jie zuó tiān zuò le yí gè dàn gāo dàn gāo hěn hǎo chī
task: Join into one sentence: "The cake my older sister made yesterday is delicious."
zh: 我姐姐昨天做的蛋糕很好吃。
py: wǒ jiě jie zuó tiān zuò de dàn gāo hěn hǎo chī
en: The cake my older sister made yesterday is delicious.
why: The relative clause drops 了 and the counted object, and ends in 的 before 蛋糕. The time word may sit before or after the subject.

src: 我有两个朋友，他们都在上海工作。
src_py: wǒ yǒu liǎng gè péng you tā men dōu zài shàng hǎi gōng zuò
task: Say it as one sentence: "Two of my friends both work in Shanghai."
zh: 我的两个朋友都在上海工作。
py: wǒ de liǎng gè péng you dōu zài shàng hǎi gōng zuò
en: Two of my friends both work in Shanghai.
why: Owner + 的 comes before the number and measure word: 我的两个朋友. The owner never goes after the measure word.

src: 我在商店里买了一件衣服，衣服很漂亮。
src_py: wǒ zài shāng diàn lǐ mǎi le yī jiàn yī fu yī fu hěn piào liang
task: Join into one sentence: "I bought a very pretty dress in the shop."
zh: 我在商店里买了一件很漂亮的衣服。
py: wǒ zài shāng diàn lǐ mǎi le yī jiàn hěn piào liang de yī fu
en: I bought a very pretty piece of clothing in the shop.
why: The description 很漂亮 + 的 moves in front of 衣服. 一件 normally comes first, though the spoken order 很漂亮的一件衣服 also occurs.

src_py: zhè shì bà ba mǎi de chē
task: Drop the noun: "This is the one Dad bought."
zh: 这是爸爸买的。
py: zhè shì bà ba mǎi de
en: This is the one Dad bought.
why: With 车 understood, the clause 爸爸买 + 的 stands for 'the one Dad bought'. 的 cannot be dropped with the noun.

s_py: nǐ kàn jiàn xiǎo wáng shū bāo le ma
zh: 你看见小王的书包了吗？
py: nǐ kàn jiàn xiǎo wáng de shū bāo le ma
en: Have you seen Xiao Wang's school bag?
why: A named owner before an ordinary thing needs 的: 小王的书包. Without it 小王 and 书包 do not link.

s_py: tā shì yí gè hěn hǎo lǎo shī
zh: 她是一个很好的老师。
py: tā shì yí gè hěn hǎo de lǎo shī
en: She is a very good teacher.
why: 很好 is a phrase, so 的 must link it to 老师. 好老师 would be fine, but 很好老师 is not.

s: 这儿是一个很安静地方。
s_py: zhè r shì yī gè hěn ān jìng dì fang
zh: 这儿是一个很安静的地方。
py: zhè r shì yī gè hěn ān jìng de dì fang
en: This is a very quiet place.
why: 很安静 is a degree word + adjective, a phrase, so 的 must link it to 地方: 很安静的地方. Without 的 it does not attach to the noun.

s_py: xǐ huan hē chá rén hěn duō
zh: 喜欢喝茶的人很多。
py: xǐ huan hē chá de rén hěn duō
en: There are many people who like drinking tea.
why: The verb phrase 喜欢喝茶 describes 人, so it must close with 的: 喜欢喝茶的人.

s: 坐在我旁边人是我同学。
s_py: zuò zài wǒ páng biān rén shì wǒ tóng xué
zh: 坐在我旁边的人是我同学。
py: zuò zài wǒ páng biān de rén shì wǒ tóng xué
en: The person sitting next to me is my classmate.
why: The clause 坐在我旁边 describes 人, so it must end in 的 right before the noun. Without 的 the clause and 人 do not link.

s_py: zhè ge shǒu jī bú shì wǒ
zh: 这个手机不是我的。
py: zhè ge shǒu jī bú shì wǒ de
en: This phone is not mine.
why: Dropping the noun must not drop 的. 我 alone would mean 'me', so 'mine' is 我的.

s: 这把伞是我的，那把是姐姐。
s_py: zhè bǎ sǎn shì wǒ de nà bǎ shì jiě jie
zh: 这把伞是我的，那把是姐姐的。
py: zhè bǎ sǎn shì wǒ de nà bǎ shì jiě jie de
en: This umbrella is mine, and that one is my sister's.
why: With the noun 伞 understood, 姐姐的 means 'my sister's'. Without 的 the sentence says that the umbrella is my sister herself.

s_py: liǎng gè wǒ de péng you lái le
zh: 我的两个朋友来了。
py: wǒ de liǎng gè péng you lái le
en: Two of my friends came.
why: The owner goes first, then number + measure + noun. English 'two of my friends' cannot be copied in that order.

s_py: wǒ mǎi le sān běn de shū
zh: 我买了三本书。
py: wǒ mǎi le sān běn shū
en: I bought three books.
why: A number + measure word attaches to the noun directly. 的 after 本 is never used.

s_py: zhè ge de rén shì shuí
zh: 这个人是谁？
py: zhè ge rén shì shuí
en: Who is this person?
why: 这个 already points at the noun, so nothing goes between it and 人. 的 after a measure word is a classic error.

s: 我有一些的问题想问你。
s_py: wǒ yǒu yī xiē de wèn tí xiǎng wèn nǐ
zh: 我有一些问题想问你。
py: wǒ yǒu yī xiē wèn tí xiǎng wèn nǐ
en: I have some questions I want to ask you.
why: 一些 acts like a number + measure word and takes no 的 before the noun.

s_py: wǒ de mā ma shì yī shēng
zh: 我的妈妈是医生。
py: wǒ de mā ma shì yī shēng
en: My mother is a doctor.
why: Many learners think 的 must be dropped, but 我的妈妈 is grammatical. It sounds heavier than 我妈妈, and the sentence is correct.

s: 我哥哥的朋友住在我们学校旁边。
s_py: wǒ gē ge de péng you zhù zài wǒ men xué xiào páng biān
zh: 我哥哥的朋友住在我们学校旁边。
py: wǒ gē ge de péng you zhù zài wǒ men xué xiào páng biān
en: My older brother's friend lives next to our school.
why: The chain drops 的 after the pronouns and keeps it on the last link before 朋友. Both 我哥哥 and 我们学校 are normal as given.

s_py: tā shì wǒ zuì hǎo de péng you
zh: 他是我最好的朋友。
py: tā shì wǒ zuì hǎo de péng you
en: He is my best friend.
why: 最好 is a phrase, so 的 stays before 朋友. Learners may want to drop it after 好 alone, but with 最 it is required.

s_py: wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī běn xīn shū
zh: 我想买一本新书。
py: wǒ xiǎng mǎi yī běn xīn shū
en: I want to buy a new book.
why: A one-syllable adjective sits directly before the noun: 新书. 的 is not needed in this neutral description.

s: 这是我们第一次见面的地方。
s_py: zhè shì wǒ men dì yī cì jiàn miàn de dì fang
zh: 这是我们第一次见面的地方。
py: zhè shì wǒ men dì yī cì jiàn miàn de dì fang
en: This is the place where we first met.
why: The clause 我们第一次见面 ends in 的 before 地方. There is no separate word for 'where', and the order is correct.

s_py: bīng xiāng lǐ méi yǒu chī de
zh: 冰箱里没有吃的。
py: bīng xiāng lǐ méi yǒu chī de
en: There is nothing to eat in the fridge.
why: 吃的 means 'something to eat', with 的 standing for the missing noun. Dropping 的 would leave a bare verb as an object.

s_py: tā de nà běn cí diǎn hěn yǒu yòng
zh: 他的那本词典很有用。
py: tā de nà běn cí diǎn hěn yǒu yòng
en: That dictionary of his is very useful.
why: Owner + 的, then 那 + measure + noun: 他的那本词典. 的 after 他 is fine, and no 的 follows 本.

s: 这是一部两个小时的电影，我们看完要九点了。
s_py: zhè shì yī bù liǎng gè xiǎo shí de diàn yǐng wǒ men kàn wán yào jiǔ diǎn le
zh: 这是一部两个小时的电影，我们看完要九点了。
py: zhè shì yī bù liǎng gè xiǎo shí de diàn yǐng wǒ men kàn wán yào jiǔ diǎn le
en: This is a two-hour film, and it will be nine o'clock when we finish.
why: An amount that describes the kind of thing, like 两个小时的电影, does keep 的. It sits after 一部, so 的 does not directly follow a measure word.

s: 我在公园里认识了一个很会照顾孩子的邻居。
s_py: wǒ zài gōng yuán lǐ rèn shi le yí gè hěn huì zhào gù hái zi de lín ju
zh: 我在公园里认识了一个很会照顾孩子的邻居。
py: wǒ zài gōng yuán lǐ rèn shi le yí gè hěn huì zhào gù hái zi de lín ju
en: I met a neighbour in the park who is very good at looking after children.
why: 一个 comes first and the long clause + 的 sits right before 邻居. The sentence follows the number + description + 的 + noun order.
